article_title: Cursor Adds Remote Control: Its iOS App Can Now View and Message Local Agents Running on a Paired Computer

content_preview.title: Cursor Adds Remote Control: Its iOS App Can Now View and Message Local Agents Running on a Paired Computer
content_preview.summary: Cursor's iOS app can now list and message agents running on a paired computer. The agents stay local, so the machine must remain on and online.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Cursor has added a Remote Control feature that lets users monitor and message coding agents running on their own computer from a phone. According to the [Cursor changelog entry dated Oct 6, 2026](https://cursor.com/changelog/remote-control-local-agents), "You can now see and reply to the local agents running on your computer from the Cursor iOS app."

editor_notes.content_quality: Concise Briefing (464 words, within the 300-800 policy range; title 106 characters, under the 150 cap). Clear Overview / What We Know / Context / What We Don't Know structure. Title ('View and Message Local Agents Running on a Paired Computer') matches the Cursor changelog: 'see and reply to the local agents running on your computer from the Cursor iOS app' and 'Tap one to see what it's doing or send it a message'; pairing is 'approve your pairing request in the Cursor desktop app'. The article does not claim that Remote Control starts agents or approves actions, and the changelog says neither.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all three snapshots from disk via gunzip (source-0/1/2.html.gz); manifest has status 200 for all and suspicious_patterns null for all three. source-0 (cursor.com/changelog/remote-control-local-agents): snapshot contains the 'Oct 6, 2026' entry titled 'Remote control for local agents'. Confirmed verbatim: the quoted sentence in the Overview; on by default for everyone except Enterprise organizations; download iOS app and sign in, computers appear automatically, tap computer and approve pairing request in desktop app; local agents list, tap to see what it's doing or send a message; 'Remote control doesn't move your agents anywhere... Your computer needs to stay on and online'; 'Keep this computer awake' setting and plugged-in/lid-open requirement. No platform other than iOS, no security/encryption statement and no plan list beyond Enterprise are given. The snapshot ALSO states 'Enterprise admins can turn it on in Org settings > Security and identity > Remote control' - which contradicts one claim in 'What We Don't Know' (see concerns). source-1 (cursor.com/changelog/self-hosted-machines, Sep 2, 2026 entry present): supports 'keep tool execution entirely in your own network' (verbatim in substance); article cites it only for that background, appropriately. source-2 (code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control): confirmed 'The web and mobile interfaces are a window into that local session, so your computer has to stay on and the claude process has to keep running'; 'available on Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans. API keys are not supported'; connects claude.ai/code or the Claude app (iOS and Android) to a local session; 'the session transcript, including your messages, Claude's responses, and tool activity, is stored on Anthropic servers' while connected. The Anthropic claims are attributed to Anthropic and not endorsed on trust; the comparison ('resembles one that Anthropic documents') does not say Cursor copied or competes. Allowlist confirmed: cursor.com (line 801) and code.claude.com (line 2689) in config/source_allowlist.txt. Internal link /article/2026-09/26-cursor-launches-rollouts-and-security-reviewer-bots-built-on-its-firetiger-acquisition resolves to an existing article. PR branch contains exactly one new file (the submission) on top of the main merge-base; hash and signature valid per chief:review.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All claims in Overview, What We Know and Context trace to the sources. One error in a subordinate bullet of What We Don't Know: it says the entry does not say 'whether administrators will be able to enable it' for Enterprise organizations, but the changelog states 'Enterprise admins can turn it on in Org settings > Security and identity > Remote control.' The omission of this fact from What We Know is also a completeness gap. The reason for the exclusion is indeed not given. Remaining 'don't know' items (Android, browser, message transport/data storage) are accurate: the entry is silent on them.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral, attributed, no promotional language or AI self-reference. Because the Claude Code docs are Anthropic's own claims, the article attributes them explicitly and applies no extra credit.
editor_notes.originality: No existing article covers Cursor Remote Control. Closest prior items: the 2026-09/26 Cursor Rollouts and Security Review article (different feature, linked as prior coverage) and the 2026-10/03 VS Code 1.140 remote delegation article (different product). No duplication. No independent outlet coverage is cited; the article is explicit that it relies on first-party sources.
concerns: 'What We Don't Know' wrongly states the changelog does not say whether Enterprise administrators can enable Remote Control; the changelog says admins can turn it on under Org settings > Security and identity > Remote control. Single subordinate error, covered by a correction.
Sourcing is entirely first-party (vendor changelog and vendor docs); no independent verification exists, as the article discloses.
recommendations: Include the Enterprise admin opt-in path in What We Know and drop the admin question from What We Don't Know.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively accurate, well sourced Briefing with one recoverable subordinate error outside the headline, summary and lead. APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS with a single correction.
